theme: I and the Father are one; Lazarus raised
readingInstruction: Read John 10:22-11:57. Jesus declares that he and the Father are one, and then raises Lazarus from the dead. Notice how the raising of Lazarus both displays his glory and sets his death in motion.
settingTheScene: It is winter, at the Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah), which celebrated the cleansing of the temple. The Jews press Jesus to say plainly whether he is the Christ. His answer leads to a second attempt to stone him. He withdraws across the Jordan, and then receives word that his friend Lazarus, in Bethany near Jerusalem, is sick. The seventh and greatest sign in John’s Gospel follows.
observation: “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me” (10:27).
“I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand” (10:28).
“I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live” (11:25).
“It is better for you that one man should die for the people, not that the whole nation should perish” (11:50).
interpretation:
“If you are the Christ, tell us plainly,” they say. Jesus replies that he has told them, and his works testify, but they do not believe because they are not among his sheep. Then he gives some of the most comforting words in the Bible. His sheep hear his voice. He knows them, and they follow him. He gives them eternal life. They will never perish, and no one can snatch them out of his hand. Then he says the Father’s hand holds them too: “No one is able to snatch them out of the Father’s hand.” This is the security of every believer. Salvation is held by God, not by the strength of our grip. And then: “I and the Father are one.” The Jews pick up stones, for they understand he is claiming to be God.

When word comes that Lazarus is ill, Jesus waits two more days. This looks like neglect, but he explains that the illness is for the glory of God. When he arrives, Lazarus has been dead four days. Martha meets him and says, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” Jesus says, “Your brother will rise again.” She believes in the resurrection at the last day. Then Jesus says, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and everyone who lives and believes in me shall never die.” He asks, “Do you believe this?” Martha answers with one of the great confessions: “Yes, Lord; I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God.”

When Mary comes weeping, Jesus is deeply moved in spirit and troubled. Then comes the shortest verse in the English Bible: “Jesus wept.” The Son of God, who knows he is about to raise Lazarus, weeps with those who weep. He is not distant from our grief. At the tomb he prays aloud for the sake of the crowd and cries, “Lazarus, come out!” The dead man comes out, bound in grave clothes. “Unbind him, and let him go.”

The sign brings belief to many, but the chief priests and Pharisees decide that Jesus must die. Caiaphas, the high priest, says unwittingly that it is better for one man to die for the people. John comments that he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and to gather into one the children of God who are scattered abroad. The miracle that gave life to Lazarus will lead to the death of Jesus. The giver of life gives his own.
connection: Psalm 23 and Ezekiel 34 are the background to the sheep imagery. Isaiah 25:8 promises that God will swallow up death forever. Daniel 12:2 speaks of those who sleep in the dust awakening. Hosea 13:14 says God will ransom them from the power of Sheol. 1 Corinthians 15:20-26 speaks of Christ’s resurrection as the firstfruits. 1 Thessalonians 4:13-18 comforts those grieving believers. Romans 8:35-39 speaks of the security of those loved by Christ. Hebrews 4:15 says we have a high priest who sympathizes with our weaknesses.
application:
Rest in verses 28 and 29. Your salvation is held in the hands of Christ and the Father.

Bring your grief to Jesus, who wept. Tell him what you have lost.

Ask Martha’s question of yourself: “Do you believe this?” Answer it in your own words.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus that no one can snatch you from his hand.
Ask him to help you hear his voice.
Thank him that he and the Father are one.
